newsitem.title: USA: Maxwell House denies coffee plant closure.
newsitem.headline: Maxwell House denies coffee plant closure.

text.p: Maxwell House, a division of Philip Morris Co Inc Kraft Foods, denied on Thursday rumours that its Jacksonville, Florida, coffee roasting plant had temporarily closed due to a shortage in coffee supplies.
"The story is not true regarding the closing of our plant," said Dave Jolson, director of coffee purchasing at Maxwell House.

But another Kraft Foods spokeswoman confirmed the company had temporarily halted production of flavored General Foods International coffee at the Jacksonville plant, for "normal maintenance and cleaning."
"That is a temporary shutdown for seven to 10 days," said Kraft Foods spokeswoman Nancy Daigler. "But I can definitely tell you that the facility as a whole is up and running."
Daigler said operations were normal at Maxwell House's roasting facilities in Houston, Texas, and San Leandro, California.
Mounting concern about supply availability has sent coffee prices soaring once again in the past week, boosting the nearby futures by some 10 percent in the past week.
Near-term supply tightness is especially acute, dealers said, coming just as roasters move into their heaviest processing period ahead of winter.
"Roasters are screaming and screaming for their coffee and nobody can come up with it," one coffee trader said.
"They cannot buy large quantities of coffee on the spot because nobody has it."
Traders said supply woes are likely to persist until fresh beans from begin to arrive from Latin America toward the end of the year.
-- Patricia Avidan, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640
